questions.solution_text:
Multiply both sides by $3$: $|4x + 2| = 18$.
Case 1: $4x + 2 = 18 \implies 4x = 16 \implies x = 4$
Case 2: $4x + 2 = -18 \implies 4x = -20 \implies x = -5$
Check $x = 4$: $\left|\dfrac{4(4) + 2}{3}\right| = \left|\dfrac{18}{3}\right| = 6$, valid.
Check $x = -5$: $\left|\dfrac{4(-5) + 2}{3}\right| = \left|\dfrac{-18}{3}\right| = 6$, valid.
So $x = 4$ or $x = -5$.

Case 1: $4x-3=2-x \implies 5x=5 \implies x=1$.
Case 2: $4x-3=-(2-x) \implies 4x-3=-2+x \implies 3x=1 \implies x=\frac13$.
Check $x=1$: $|4(1)-3|=1$ and $2-1=1$, valid.
Check $x=\frac13$: $\left|4\left(\frac13\right)-3\right|=\frac53$ and $2-\frac13=\frac53$, valid.
So $x=1$ or $x=\frac13$.
